title: XOR a whole list
hook: Seven numbers, one operation, folded left to right. What is left at the end?

doesNotKnow: that a XOR a is 0 and a XOR 0 is a
that XOR ignores order, so one pass finds the lone value

misconception: Finding the one number without a partner in a list needs sorting or a table of counts.
objective: The learner can fold 5 3 3 4 7 5 4 with XOR one number at a time, see the second 3 switch back the lamps the first 3 switched (6 back to 5), see a second order also end at 7, and explain why (a XOR a = 0, a XOR 0 = a, order does not matter).

claims.text: Folding 5 3 3 4 7 5 4 with XOR from 0 gives 7, written 111 in binary (running values 5, 6, 5, 1, 6, 3, 7). Their sum is 31.
claims.source: Demo.tsx xorAll(BASE) and the stage's running value; builder's node run 2026-10-14: running 5,6,5,1,6,3,7; sum 31 (distractor option).

claims.text: Whatever lamps a number flips, its partner flips the same lamps back: a XOR a = 0, and a XOR 0 = a. On stage the second 3 (011) flips lamps 2 and 1 back and the running value goes from 6 to 5, as before the first 3.
claims.source: Bitwise: each bit of a XOR a is b XOR b = 0; each bit of a XOR 0 is b. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Algebra true, mechanism sentence false on the stage's own order. Trace of 7 3 5 4 5 3 4: 3 turns lamps 2 and 1 OFF (111->100) and its partner turns them back ON (000->011); the first 5 turns 4 off and 1 on. So 'the bits it switched on switch back off' (and the reveal's 'the lamps it had switched on switched back off') misdescribes what the learner watches. Fix (builder): 'the lamps it flipped flip back' / 'its partner flips the same lamps again'. · Builder 2026-10-14 (W-203): reworded per pass 21; awaiting re-check. | FC pass 23 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. The reveal (line 168) and the Demo header now use this wording. A number flips exactly the lamps where it has a 1 (r XOR (r XOR v) = v). The partner flips the same set again, which cancels the flip whatever lies between them, because toggles commute. Own trace of 7 3 5 4 5 3 4: each fold flips the lamps of v's bits (3 flips 2,1; 5 flips 4,1; 4 flips 4), and the end is 111. The pass 21 objection (on versus off) no longer applies: the text says 'flips', not 'switched on'. a XOR a = 0 and a XOR 0 = a hold bitwise. | v3: stage message for a twin fold: 'the second 3 flips lamps 2 and 1 back, as the first did'; lamps flipped by the last number are ringed.

claims.text: XOR ignores order, so any order of the list ends at 7; the learner's second order (the first 'New order' is 7 3 4 5 4 3 5) also ends at 7.
claims.source: XOR is associative and commutative (bitwise addition mod 2). The stage's 'New order' button reshuffles with mulberry32 seeds 1001, 1002, ... (seeds not chosen to show anything; every order gives 7). Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): XOR is commutative and associative; stage reshuffle uses mulberry32(1000 + k), k = 1, 2, ... (seeds 1001, 1002, ... as stated); all 200 orders tried give 7. | v3: v3 list 5 3 3 4 7 5 4; New order uses mulberry32(1001) for the first reshuffle (seed not chosen for the result; every order gives 7). Builder's node run: 7 3 4 5 4 3 5 -> 7.

claims.text: It needs every other number to appear an even number of times; one that appears three times does not cancel.
claims.source: The XOR of a list is the XOR of the values that appear an odd number of times (pairs cancel by c2). A value appearing 3 times leaves one copy, so the result is lone XOR that value. Node example: 5 5 5 7 7 gives 5, and 5 5 5 7 2 2 gives 2, not 7. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): node: 5 5 5 7 7 -> 5; 5 5 5 7 2 2 -> 2. Derivation (result = XOR of odd-count values) holds. | v3: v3: 'and spoils the answer' dropped.

claims.text: Finding the lone number this way takes one pass, with no sorting and no table of counts.
claims.source: One XOR per element, one running value of storage. Unverified. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): One XOR per element, one running value; no sort, no counts (true of Demo.tsx xorAll and of the method).

recall.question: A list holds 1,001 numbers. Every number appears exactly twice except one. You XOR all of them together. What is left?
options: It depends on the order of the list
recall.why: Each pair XORs to 0 (a XOR a = 0), XOR ignores order, and the lone number XOR 0 is itself.
